hook.text: Gasoline is one of the most energy-dense liquids we use—a gallon holds as much energy as 33 kWh.

buildup.text: It's refined from crude oil. Different grades (87, 91, 93) refer to octane—resistance to premature ignition.

discovery.text: Higher octane lets engines compress fuel more before igniting, which extracts more power per stroke.

twist.text: Most cars are tuned for regular 87. Using premium in them wastes money—the engine can't use the difference.

climax.text: Gasoline engines only convert about 30% of fuel energy into motion. The rest becomes heat.

punchline.text: Your engine wastes most of every gallon as heat.

quiz.question: What does a gasoline's octane rating measure?

details.summary: Gasoline is a refined petroleum product containing hydrocarbons that release energy when ignited. Its octane rating indicates resistance to premature detonation inside the engine's cylinders.
details.whyItMatters: Using the correct octane fuel prevents engine knock, which can cause damage over time. Understanding fuel helps drivers make informed choices at the pump and protect their engines.
takeaways: Gasoline is a mix of hydrocarbons distilled from crude oil
Octane rating measures resistance to premature ignition

faq.question: Does premium gasoline make a regular car faster?
faq.answer: If your engine is designed for regular fuel, premium provides no benefit. The engine cannot use the extra knock resistance. Only cars that specify premium will see improved performance from higher octane.

faq.question: What causes the smell of gasoline?
faq.answer: Volatile hydrocarbons like benzene and toluene evaporate easily at room temperature, releasing the characteristic strong odor. Modern fuel systems are sealed to minimize these evaporative emissions.
